- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.description: Trace profile image serving code path
input.prompt:
In this repository, find the code path for a browser HTTP request that fetches another user's profile image (avatar). I need to trace the full chain from the HTTP route/handler that serves the image, through any service/controller layers, down to the data layer (database query or file storage lookup) that retrieves the actual image data/URL.

Search for terms like: "avatar", "profile image", "profile picture", "profilePicture", "avatarUrl", "image" combined with "user" or "profile", routes serving images, S3/storage clients, etc.

For each hop in the chain, report:
- The symbol name (function/method/class/route handler)
- The file path (relative to repo root)

Order them from the entry point (HTTP route handler that receives the browser request) down to the lowest-level data access (DB query, ORM call, storage bucket read, etc.). Include every intermediate hop (controller -> service -> repository/DAO -> data layer).

If there are multiple candidate features (e.g. multiple apps/services in a monorepo), pick the one most clearly related to "user profile image" serving to other users (e.g. viewing another user's avatar), and note if there are alternatives.

Report back concisely with the exact chain, each hop as "symbol — file_path", plus any relevant line numbers if easy to get.

This is the memos (usememos/memos) repo, and this is the only avatar-serving path found (single app, no other services/frontends serving avatars to other users).

## Chain: HTTP request for another user's avatar (memos repo)

1. **Route registration** — `(*FileServerService).RegisterRoutes` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`
   `fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)`

2. **HTTP handler (entry point)** — `serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168-210`
   Auth-gates anonymous access, reads `:identifier` path param, fetches the target user, extracts image bytes from the stored data URI, and streams the response.

3. **Controller helper: user lookup** — `getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-717`
   Calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`.

4. **Controller helper: image decode** — `parseDataURI` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737` (uses `dataURIRegex` at line 98)
   Decodes the base64 data URI stored on the user record into MIME type + raw bytes.

5. **Store/service layer** — `(*Store).GetUser` — `store/user.go:148-168`
   Checks an in-memory user cache by ID (avatar lookups by username skip the cache), otherwise delegates to `ListUsers`.

6. **Store/service layer** — `(*Store).ListUsers` — `store/user.go:136-146`
   Calls the DB driver's `ListUsers`, then populates the cache.

7. **Data layer (DB driver)** — `(*DB).ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88-205`
   Builds a raw SQL query filtering by username and runs `d.db.QueryContext(ctx, query, args...)` against the `user` table, `SELECT`ing the `avatar_url` column (line 159) and scanning it into `user.AvatarURL` (line 189).
   Note: equivalent driver implementations exist for Postgres (`store/db/postgres/user.go`) and MySQL (`store/db/mysql/user.go`) — sqlite is the default/most common driver but the same query shape is duplicated across all three.

Notes on data model: memos stores avatars inline as base64 data URIs in the `user.avatar_url` column (no S3/file-storage lookup for avatars — that path only exists for memo *attachments*, via `internal/storage/s3` and `serveAttachmentFile`/`serveMediaStream` in the same file). If the user intended attachment/resource files (not avatars) as the target, that's the alternative candidate chain, rooted at `serveAttachmentFile` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:132`) → `store.GetAttachment` → driver `GetAttachment`/local disk or S3 (`internal/storage/s3`).</result>

content.text:
h07.

Chain for a browser request fetching another user's profile avatar (memos repo — `usememos/memos`):

`(*FileServerService).RegisterRoutes` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (registers `GET /users/:identifier/avatar`)
`serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
`getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
`parseDataURI` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737
`(*Store).GetUser` — store/user.go:148
`(*Store).ListUsers` — store/user.go:136
`(*DB).ListUsers` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (raw SQL `SELECT ... avatar_url FROM user`, `d.db.QueryContext`)

Notes:
- Avatars are stored inline as base64 data URIs in the `user.avatar_url` column — no separate blob storage for avatars.
- Equivalent driver implementations exist for Postgres (`store/db/postgres/user.go`) and MySQL (`store/db/mysql/user.go`); sqlite is the default.
- A separate chain exists for memo *attachments* (not avatars), rooted at `serveAttachmentFile` (fileserver.go:132) going through `store.GetAttachment` to local disk or S3 (`internal/storage/s3`) — not applicable if the question is specifically about profile images.
